name: New Jersey
overview: New Jersey combines ANCHOR, Senior Freeze and Stay NJ with an alternative income-tax property deduction or refundable credit. Benefits require explicit timing and overlap rules.

programs.name: ANCHOR
programs.ageRule: All ages; renter amount increases at age 65.
programs.incomeDefinition: 2025 NJ-1040 line 29 income, with application instructions for nonfilers.
programs.incomeLimits: Owners up to $250,000; renters up to $150,000.
programs.maximumBenefit: 2025-benefit table: homeowners $1,500 at income ≤ $150,000, $1,000 above that to $250,000; renters $450 under 65 or $700 age 65+.
programs.formulaSummary: Fixed income/tenure tiers rather than a tax-to-income threshold.
programs.application: ANCHOR application or combined PAS-1 where required; eligible groups may be automatically enrolled.
eligibilityNotes: Ordinary rental housing generally must be property-tax subject; specific PILOT rules differ for renters and owners.
interactions: An unclaimed $50 income-tax property credit for an eligible senior nonfiler may be included in the ANCHOR payment; it is not an additional separate credit.
Owner benefits coordinate with Senior Freeze, Stay NJ and other covered property relief.
programs.programYear: 2025 circumstances and income; ANCHOR payments begin September 2026.

sources.title: How ANCHOR benefits are calculated (2025 tax year)

programs.name: Senior Freeze (Property Tax Reimbursement)
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ or receiving qualifying Social Security/Railroad Retirement disability by December 31, 2025.
programs.incomeDefinition: Total annual program income, including specified nontaxable Social Security, retirement and other additions.
programs.incomeLimits: 2024 income ≤ $168,268 and 2025 income ≤ $172,475; limited base-year retention exception applies.
programs.maximumBenefit: Qualifying property-tax increase above established base-year tax.
programs.formulaSummary: Reimburse the eligible difference between current and base-year property taxes, subject to eligibility and coordination.
eligibilityNotes: Own and occupy since December 31, 2022 through December 31, 2025, with listed exceptions.
Qualifying mobile-home owners can use 18% of site fees.
interactions: Base-year taxes affect the separate income-tax property deduction/credit.
Total covered property-tax relief, including ANCHOR and Stay NJ, cannot exceed property taxes paid.

programs.name: Stay NJ
programs.ageRule: At least one qualifying spouse age 65+ during 2025.
programs.incomeDefinition: Senior Freeze total annual income definition.
programs.incomeLimits: Current 2025-tax-year benefit: income ≤ $200,000 under FY 2027 budget.
programs.maximumBenefit: Annualized 2027 caps: $6,500 at income ≤ $100,000; $5,000 above $100,000 to $150,000; $4,000 above $150,000 to $200,000. Annualization assumes no FY 2028 change.
programs.formulaSummary: Relief targets 50% of qualifying property taxes, subject to income-tier caps and coordination with ANCHOR/Senior Freeze; appropriations control payable installments.
eligibilityNotes: Own and occupy for all 12 months of 2025.
Renters and mobile-home owners excluded; eligible PILOT owners may qualify.
interactions: ANCHOR and Senior Freeze reduce the remaining Stay NJ payment under the applicable benefit statement. Total covered relief cannot exceed property taxes paid.
programs.programYear: New Jersey schedules payments for tax-year-2025 benefits for February and May 2027. Annualized caps assume no FY 2028 change.

sources.title: Stay NJ — current 2025 tax-year rules, updated November 12, 2026

programs.name: Income-Tax Property Tax Credit
programs.incomeDefinition: New Jersey gross income and filing-status thresholds.
programs.incomeLimits: Ordinarily income above filing threshold; below-threshold claimants must meet age 65, blindness or disability conditions.
programs.maximumBenefit: $50; $25 for separate-return spouses sharing the residence; part-year proration applies.
programs.formulaSummary: Flat refundable alternative to the property-tax deduction.
eligibilityNotes: Qualifying New Jersey principal residence; renters use 18% of rent as property tax.
interactions: Senior Freeze applicants use base-year tax rules.
A credit included in ANCHOR is not paid a second time.

sources.title: Property tax deduction/credit eligibility and coordination

programs.name: Income-Tax Property Tax Deduction
programs.incomeLimits: Gross income above $20,000, or above $10,000 for single or married/CU separate filers. At or below those thresholds, eligible older, blind or disabled residents may claim the credit only.
programs.maximumBenefit: Deduct up to $15,000 of qualifying property tax; deduction amount is not tax savings.
programs.formulaSummary: Reduce taxable income by eligible property tax or 18% of rent, subject to cap and split/proration rules.
programs.application: NJ-1040 Worksheet H selects the better deduction or credit.
eligibilityNotes: Same principal-residence qualification as the credit alternative.
interactions: Senior Freeze changes the allowable tax base.

sources.title: Property tax deduction/credit eligibility and coordination

laterChanges: The FY 2027 Appropriations Act lowers the Stay NJ income ceiling from $500,000 to $200,000 for tax-year-2025 benefits and sets the applicable payment caps.
researchNotes: Tax year, payment season and state fiscal year differ. A 2025-season ANCHOR announcement does not describe the same benefit period as tax-year-2025 benefits.
The 2025 ANCHOR homeowner table does not include the earlier $250 senior homeowner addition.
Annualized Stay NJ caps depend on future appropriations; payable installments follow their budget periods.
Household amounts depend on qualifying payments, other property-tax benefits and the installments authorized by the applicable budget.
